chunk_findings.detail: The new `offset` parameter is inserted before the existing `all`, `mode`, and `sources` parameters in the public API function at this line. Any existing caller that passes `all` positionally, for example `ddflow.api.viewers.search_view(repo, query, kind, since, item, limit, True)`, now binds `True` to `offset` instead of `all`, so the call either skips the first row or raises an offset-past-end ViewError for small result sets. The new parameter should be added after `sources` or made keyword-only to avoid changing existing positional argument meaning.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `offset` parameter is accepted by `read`, whose doc says it is the one read over every viewer including `search`, but the diff only forwards `offset` to the `list_view` call at line 173. For `mode="search"`, `offset` is silently ignored: `read(repo, mode="search", limit=100, offset=500)` on a repo with >500 matches returns the first 100 rows rather than rows 500–599 and raises no error, so the advertised parameter does not work for one of the viewers it claims to cover.

chunk_findings.detail: When a list is truncated, the new hint `next page: --offset {d['next']}` omits the current `--limit`. Since `--limit` defaults to `R.LIST_DEFAULT_LIMIT` (25), a user who runs the displayed hint after a non-default limit gets a different page size. Example: `ddflow list task --limit 50` with 2720 rows prints `next page: --offset 50`; running `ddflow list task --offset 50` shows only 25 rows, not the next 50. The clamped case from the bug is equally misleading: after `--limit 5000` the hint says `next page: --offset 1000`, but running that without the clamped limit gives the default 25-row page. The hint should include `--limit {d['limit']}`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new “next page” hint only includes `--limit` and `--offset`, dropping the other filters that determined the listed rows. For example, `ddflow list task --phase ph --limit 10` with more than 10 matching tasks prints `next page: --limit 10 --offset 10`; running `ddflow list task --limit 10 --offset 10` then lists tasks across all phases, not the next page of `phase ph`. The same happens with `--all` (`ddflow list bug --all --limit 10` loses `--all` and reverts to the default narrowing). `_print_rows` receives only `kind`, `out`, and `defaulted`, so the emitted command fragment is not an equivalent next-page command for any filtered invocation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:_print_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The new truncation note unconditionally tells the caller to “page with offset={body.get('next')}”, but `next` is only added to `list_view` bodies, not to search bodies. For a truncated search response (`mode="search"`, `limit=10`, and more than 10 matches), `body.get('next')` is absent/None, so the note renders as `page with offset=None`; the change’s own triage says search offsets are refused, so there is no valid `offset` for that mode at all. The old note (“raise limit…”) was valid for search; the replacement is a broken instruction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:262

chunk_findings.detail: The MCP paging hint omits the current `limit`, so following it changes the page size. Example: a caller passes `limit=50`, receives `truncated: showing 50 of 2720; … page with offset=50 …`, then calls again with `offset=50` and no `limit`; `operations.py` defaults `limit` to 25, so the client gets 25 rows rather than the next 50. The CLI equivalent of this hint was already fixed to include `--limit N --offset M`; the MCP path was not.

chunk_findings.detail: The new paging hint says only `page with limit={body.get('limit')} offset={body['next']}` and does not tell the MCP caller to keep the other request fields (`kind`, `mode`, `phase`, `item`, `all`, `sources`, `since`) that selected the rows. Concrete failure: `bound_list({"kind": "bug", "phase": "research", "limit": 10})` with more than 10 matching bugs returns `"narrow the filters, or page with limit=10 offset=10 ..."`. A client following that instruction literally calls `bound_list({"limit": 10, "offset": 10})`, so the next page is computed over the default/unfiltered list rather than the `phase=research` bugs. This is the same filter-dropping bug that was fixed in the CLI by saying “the same command with --limit N --offset M”; the MCP note still drops the filters.

chunk_findings.detail: The CLI regression tests pass the wrong command for the first page. The bug is in `ddflow list task` (and the same test’s line 108 uses the correct `"list", "task"`), but line 96 and line 105 invoke `cli(seeded, ..., "task", "list", ...)`. When `task list` is not a registered command, `main([...])` exits non-zero; line 106 then `json.loads(out)` parses an error page and the test fails. If `task list` is a separate alias, the test does not exercise the fixed `list task` command path, so the claimed regression for `ddflow list task --limit 5000` is not actually covered.
